query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A candidate actionable cause (quality of crew service) whose effect on the overall rating/recommendation is being attributed. It is a driver/treatment, not a common cause of another treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: food_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: Another candidate service-aspect cause of the outcome. Treatment/driver, not a confounder that would need adjustment.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue
per_column.rationale: Service-aspect driver of the overall rating. A candidate treatment, not a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: disruption_handling_quality
per_column.rationale: How disruptions were handled is a candidate cause of satisfaction/recommendation. Treatment, not confounder.

per_column.name: customer_service_resolution_quality
per_column.rationale: Resolution quality is a candidate driver of the outcome. Treatment, not a common cause of another aspect and the outcome.

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Ground/check-in experience is a candidate driver of the overall rating. Treatment, not confounder.

per_column.name: ife_quality
per_column.rationale: Inflight entertainment quality is a candidate service-aspect cause of the rating. Treatment/driver.

per_column.name: cabin_class_experience_gap
per_column.rationale: The gap between class expectation and delivered experience sits ON the path from the concrete service aspects to dissatisfaction/low rating; it is a proximal (dis)satisfaction mediator rather than a common cause. Adjusting for it as a confounder would be an error.

per_column.name: service_decline_perception
per_column.rationale: A perceived-decline attitude is a near-outcome affective judgement lying between actual service and the recommendation decision. It is a mediator/proxy of the outcome, not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: service_consistency_across_legs
per_column.rationale: Consistency/inconsistency of service across legs is itself a candidate driver (or moderator) of the outcome, not a common cause of another aspect quality and the rating.

judge.rationale: The augmentation performs a fine-grained DRIVER DECOMPOSITION: it surfaces many plausible candidate treatments (crew, food, seat, disruption handling, customer-service resolution, ground service, IFE, cross-leg consistency), each an actionable aspect whose effect on the overall rating/recommendation one might attribute. However, the technical claim for causal attribution also requires CONFOUNDERS surfaced from the data -- variables that cause BOTH a given treatment and the outcome and therefore must be adjusted to avoid biased attribution. No such column was added. Genuine confounders here would be passenger/flight context such as Type of Traveller, Class, Route, or Verified status (which shape both how good a given service aspect is AND the overall rating), yet these live only in the original table and were not introduced or operationalised as adjustment variables by the operator. Worse, two added columns (cabin_class_experience_gap and service_decline_perception) are mediators / near-outcome attitudes on the causal path; treating them as confounders would over-control and induce bias. Thus the causal-estimation setup is only half-built: treatments are richly present, but the confounder-surfacing capability under test is essentially absent, so confounder_quality is very low.
